title: Petra and the Cover
premise: Felix Coldharbour, a deniable fixer for the Meridian Office—an embassy that exists on no map—receives a debt repayment for a favor he never performed: a ledger naming every asset his employers have buried. The stranger who delivered it, Petra Voss, claims Felix saved her life years ago in a city he's never visited, and now someone is killing everyone connected to that night. Hunted by both the Office and the ledger's original owners, Felix and Petra must trade the only secret worth killing for—Petra's true identity as the daughter of the Office's founder—to buy their way out alive. In the end Felix burns the Meridian Office's legitimacy to the ground, chooses exile over belonging, and walks away with Petra into a life with no cover at all.
about_author: Sable Dravenmoor spent a decade writing risk assessments for security consultancies before turning those gray memos into grayer fiction. They live off-grid in a coastal town that appears on exactly one map, and they refuse to say which.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Felix Coldharbour cleans up a diplomat's indiscretion in Vienna, establishing his methodical, unattached life. A courier delivers an envelope thanking him for saving a life in Trieste—a city he's never worked. POV: Felix. Beat: unease beneath routine; the first crack in his controlled world.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: The envelope contains a partial ledger of buried Meridian Office assets and a note: 'the rest when we meet.' Felix reports it and is ordered to burn it unread; instead he photographs two pages. POV: Felix. Beat: quiet rebellion—the fixer keeps something for himself for the first time.

chapters.title: The Woman at the Tram Stop
chapters.summary: Felix stakes out the dead-drop address from the note and spots Petra Voss watching him back. She vanishes before he can approach, leaving a tram ticket dated the night of the Trieste incident. POV: Petra. Beat: cat-and-mouse tension; she knows more about him than he does.

chapters.title: Trieste, 2011
chapters.summary: Flashback through recovered file fragments: an extraction gone wrong, a girl pulled from a burning safehouse, a fixer's face half-seen through smoke. Petra narrates her fragmented memory of that night. POV: Petra. Beat: longing for a past she can't verify; the mystery of her savior deepens.

chapters.title: Housecleaning
chapters.summary: Meridian's internal watchdog, Aldous Renner, opens a file on Felix after detecting the photograph. Felix's handler, Ilsa Brandt, warns him obliquely during a chess game. POV: Felix. Beat: paranoia tightening; loyalty revealed as a leash.

chapters.title: Two Pages Too Many
chapters.summary: A Meridian archivist who touched the ledger is found drowned in a dry apartment. Felix realizes the photograph makes him a target of both sides. He contacts Petra through the tram ticket's coded timetable. POV: Felix. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Terms of Trade
chapters.summary: In a Prague railway chapel, Petra offers the full ledger in exchange for Felix confirming what happened in Trieste—and protecting her until then. He refuses to confirm anything; they agree to a fragile alliance anyway. POV: alternating. Beat: wary negotiation; two liars recognizing each other.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Architecture
chapters.summary: Studying the pages together, they discover entries keyed to dates of operations officially never run—including one signed with the initials E.V., unknown to Felix. Petra goes pale at the name. POV: Petra. Beat: dread; her connection to the ledger is personal, not accidental.

chapters.title: Renner's Web
chapters.summary: Renner surveils Felix's flat, plants a listening device, and interviews Petra under a false pretext. She lies beautifully but leaves a thread. POV: Renner. Beat: cold menace; the hunter humanized just enough to be frightening.

chapters.title: Safehouse Rules
chapters.summary: Felix moves them to a bolt-hole in Bratislava with rules: no real names, no patterns, no trust. Petra breaks rule three by asking why he became a fixer. He answers with silence. POV: Felix. Beat: intimacy resisted; walls built higher because they're cracking.

chapters.title: E.V.
chapters.summary: Petra confesses her mother was Elena Voss, co-founder of the Meridian Office, erased from its history. The ledger may be Elena's insurance policy. Felix doesn't believe her—or doesn't want to. POV: Petra. Beat: vulnerable revelation met with suspicion; identity as burden.

chapters.title: The Buyer
chapters.summary: A third party surfaces: the Kestrel Group, private intelligence brokers, offering to buy the ledger and extract them both. Their envoy is a man Felix burned years ago. POV: Felix. Beat: temptation; the exit that costs everything.

chapters.title: Dry Apartment, Wet Truth
chapters.summary: Felix re-investigates the archivist's death and finds staging errors pointing inward—not to Kestrel, but to someone inside Meridian feeding the kill list. POV: Felix. Beat: betrayal crystallizing; the enemy wears a colleague's face.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Warning
chapters.summary: Brandt meets Felix alone, off the books, and tells him Renner has authorization to erase him if the ledger surfaces. She gives him forty-eight hours and no more. POV: Felix. Beat: grief disguised as professionalism; the institution cutting its own loose.

chapters.title: Running Patterns
chapters.summary: A transit montage across borders using tradecraft both know too well. Petra teaches Felix a trick her mother invented; he recognizes it from an old operation manual. POV: Petra. Beat: grudging admiration; inheritance passing between strangers.

chapters.title: The Archive Beneath the Chapel
chapters.summary: Following Elena's cipher, they find a hidden cache in the Prague chapel: letters, a photograph of Elena holding an infant, and the ledger's missing spine. Renner's team arrives minutes behind them. POV: alternating. Beat: discovery and pursuit colliding; the past made physical.

chapters.title: Fire Exit
chapters.summary: A brutal escape through Prague's underground; Felix takes a knife wound shielding Petra. She stitches him and finally tells the whole Trieste story—he did save her, and walked away without a word. POV: Petra. Beat: anger and gratitude fused; the debt named aloud.

chapters.title: What Felix Remembers
chapters.summary: Felix admits he suppressed the memory: the extraction was his first job, the girl was collateral he refused to abandon, and Meridian punished him for it. His cynicism was armor over shame. POV: Felix. Beat: confession; the fixer's mask comes off.

chapters.title: Kestrel's Offer, Renewed
chapters.summary: The wounded pair, cornered, hear out the Kestrel envoy: full identities, new lives, in exchange for the ledger and Petra's silence about her lineage. Felix almost says yes. POV: Felix. Beat: moral nadir; belonging offered at the price of self.

chapters.title: Renner's File on Petra
chapters.summary: Renner, reading intercepted photos, realizes who Petra is—and sees opportunity: control the founder's heir, control the Office's founding crime. He goes rogue from his own masters. POV: Renner. Beat: ambition curdling into obsession; a second antagonist born.

chapters.title: The Spine Decoded
chapters.summary: The ledger's spine reveals the final entry: not assets but a confession—Elena documented the Office's founding atrocity and hid her daughter as living testimony. Petra understands she was always the secret. POV: Petra. Beat: devastating clarity; identity reframed as evidence.

chapters.title: Split Decision
chapters.summary: Felix proposes splitting up to draw Renner off; Petra refuses to be protected again. They argue like family. Compromise: she runs the play, he runs backup. POV: alternating. Beat: partnership forged in conflict; equals at last.

chapters.title: Bait in Vienna
chapters.summary: They dangle a fake ledger handoff through old channels. Renner bites—but so does Brandt, revealing she's been playing a deeper game all along. POV: Felix. Beat: trap within trap; allies and enemies swap masks mid-scene.

chapters.title: Brandt's Game
chapters.summary: Brandt corners Felix: she's been building a case against the Office's current director for years and needs Elena's confession as the keystone. Help her, and Petra lives. POV: Brandt. Beat: uneasy triangulation; even loyalty here is transactional.

chapters.title: The Director
chapters.summary: Introduction of Director Casimir Hale, Elena's former partner, who signed the order that erased her. He learns Petra lives and orders the list accelerated. POV: Hale. Beat: quiet, courteous evil; the theme of inheritance embodied in its ugliest form.

chapters.title: Safehouse Burned
chapters.summary: Renner finds the Bratislava bolt-hole; the pair escape with seconds to spare but lose the physical cache, keeping only scans. Felix's wound reopens. POV: Petra. Beat: loss and desperation; everything now rides on nerve.

chapters.title: The Forty-Eight Hours
chapters.summary: Brandt's deadline expires; Meridian formally disavows Felix. His bank accounts, passports, and history begin dissolving in real time. POV: Felix. Beat: erasure; a man watching his own identity deleted.

chapters.title: No Cover
chapters.summary: Stripped of covers, Felix and Petra hide as ordinary people in a boarding house—first time either has lived without a role. A quiet chapter: market queues, bad coffee, almost-laughter. POV: alternating. Beat: tenderness; belonging found in powerlessness.

chapters.title: Hale's Proposal
chapters.summary: Hale contacts Petra directly: surrender the confession, and he'll restore Felix's existence and fund her disappearance forever. He speaks of her mother with genuine love, which makes it worse. POV: Petra. Beat: seduction of erasure; the devil quoting family.

chapters.title: What Petra Decides
chapters.summary: Petra tells Felix she intends to take the meeting—not to trade the confession away, but to confront Hale with it publicly at the Office's anniversary gala. Suicide or checkmate. POV: Petra. Beat: courage hardening; reclaiming inheritance as weapon.

chapters.title: Gala Preparations
chapters.summary: Brandt provides access, Kestrel provides distractions, Felix builds three exits and trusts one. Renner, now hunted by his own side, offers Felix an unstable truce. POV: Felix. Beat: tension ratcheting; every ally armed with an agenda.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Gala
chapters.summary: Petra enters Hale's marble world wearing her mother's reconstructed identity. The confession plays across the hall's screens as she walks in. Chaos, gasps, Hale's composure fracturing. POV: Petra. Beat: triumph inverted into peril; the truth detonates.

chapters.title: Checkmate, Almost
chapters.summary: Hale's guards move; Renner double-crosses everyone to seize Petra as leverage against Hale; Felix's chosen exit is compromised. Gunfire among the chandeliers. POV: Felix. Beat: climax igniting; plans dying faster than people.

chapters.title: The Founder's Room
chapters.summary: Cornered in the archive where Meridian was founded, Petra forces Hale to read Elena's final letter aloud—his own condemnation in his lover's handwriting. He breaks, ordering his men to stand down. POV: Petra. Beat: emotional climax; inheritance reclaimed, not inherited.

chapters.title: Renner's End
chapters.summary: Renner, refusing defeat, tries to burn the archive with everyone inside. Felix saves Hale—the man who erased him—because some debts aren't chosen. Renner falls. POV: Felix. Beat: costly mercy; character proven under fire.

chapters.title: Dissolution
chapters.summary: With the confession public and governments distancing themselves, the Meridian Office is quietly dissolved. Brandt hands Felix a clean passport and a warning: the trade remembers. POV: Brandt. Beat: fall of institutions; justice administered as paperwork.

chapters.title: Settlements
chapters.summary: Loose ends resolved: the archivist's family told a version of truth, Kestrel paid off with redacted pages, Hale awaiting trial he'll never survive. Felix and Petra settle accounts with each other. POV: Felix. Beat: accounting; debts honored, grudges released.

chapters.title: The Question of Belonging
chapters.summary: Petra asks Felix to come with her—not to hide, but to live. He weighs the only home he's ever known, which was a lie, against a future with no cover at all. POV: Felix. Beat: thematic resolution; identity chosen rather than assigned.

chapters.title: Exile, Together
chapters.summary: They leave by ferry under names that are finally, boringly real. Petra carries Elena's letters; Felix carries nothing. Somewhere behind them, the last Meridian file closes. POV: alternating. Beat: release; exile transformed into freedom.

chapters.title: One Map Only
chapters.summary: Epilogue in a coastal town off most maps: Petra teaching, Felix fixing nothing but a neighbor's roof. An envelope arrives—blank except for a tram ticket. They laugh, and burn it unread. POV: Petra. Beat: peace earned, vigilance kept; the story closes on choice.
